content.passage: My name is Radwan, and I work as a firefighter in Alexandria. Many people think our job is just putting out fires, but it’s much more than that. We rescue people from car accidents, help during floods, and sometimes save animals trapped in dangerous places. The truth is, our work can be risky. I have entered burning buildings where smoke made it hard to see and breathe. I’ve stood on shaking ladders in the middle of the night, with the heat almost burning my skin. Sadly, I have also seen lives lost before we could reach them. These moments stay with me forever. Yet, we do it because we believe in obligation – the duty to help each other, no matter the cost. In every emergency, we must act quickly, stay calm, and trust our training. We don’t think about fear in those moments; we think about the people waiting for us. I am proud to serve my community. I know that my work saves lives, and that is worth every risk. When you help others, you are not just doing a job – you are protecting hope itself.
